name: Change: Rate, Accumulation, and Flow
truth: Things change. Change accumulates. Accumulation flows.

formula: rate = rise / h; total += f(x) * width; position += direction(position, time) * speed * delta
demonstration: Watch a tangent line slide along a curve and read its slope. Pump up the count on a Riemann sum and watch rectangles converge into a continuous integral. Release particles into a vector field and watch them flow. Take over the catalyst and sustain its contact on a target â€” accumulation made bracelet-felt.
description: The calculus substrate, made visible. Change as instantaneous rate (derivative); accumulation as continuous addition (integral); vector field as flow at every point in space. This sequence's job is to establish the vocabulary so forces, wavefunctions, randomness, and noise can name what they're doing instead of running on an unintroduced backbone.
learning_objectives: Change as instantaneous rate: the derivative; slope of a curve at a point; velocity as rate of position
Slope across a curve: how slope itself becomes a function (derivative-as-function)
Accumulation as continuous addition: the integral; area under a curve; total from rate
Riemann sum: discrete accumulation approaching continuous; how rectangles become integrals in the limit
Vector fields: change-and-flow at every point in space; the first encounter with a function of space (not just time)
The fundamental theorem of calculus: change and accumulation are inverse operations; one undoes the other
Carry-forward to forces and waves: F = ma is calculus made physical; sine is the function whose second derivative is itself negated
